name: Apache HugeGraph (Server, Hubble, Loader, Computer, Vermeer, HugeGraph-AI, HugeGraph-ML, storage adapters)
tier_reason: EOIP's configured primary/reference backend; deep baseline study required by Master Prompt section 6
members: Toolchain (client, Loader, Hubble, Tools, Spark connector)
latest_version: 1.7.0 (all four component repos; master revision 1.8.0 unreleased)
license: Apache-2.0 in all repos; Docker Hub images are convenience releases, not official ASF distribution artifacts
redistribution_notes: Apache-2.0 permits redistribution and OEM use; ASF trademark rules apply to white-labelling the 'Apache HugeGraph' name, and Docker images are convenience binaries.
legal_review_reason: Low trigger: transitive dependencies (RocksDB dual Apache-2.0/GPLv2, LiteLLM enterprise directory UNVERIFIED for pinned version, CJK analyzers, cypher-for-gremlin) and ASF trademark rules need checking
community_vs_enterprise: Single Apache-2.0 distribution; no enterprise edition described in the deep dive
resolution_note: EOIP pin hugegraph/hugegraph:1.7.0 is the current release; HA compose wrongly pins PD/Store :latest and labels them enterprise images; no 1.8.0 tag yet
action_reason: Assigned Tier A; current reference backend
decision_summary: INTEGRATE as primary backend (keep behind GraphStore; move to bytecode/parameterised Gremlin, graph-per-tenant, snapshot backup); BUILD portable IR instead of the Cypher translator, EOIP ACL and vector sidecar; DEFER scale-out and MCP

name: Neo4j (Community, Enterprise, Infinigraph, GDS, Bloom, NeoDash, Aura, NVL)
tier_reason: Required EOIP backend (adapter neo4j.py, BL-03) and the market-reference labelled property graph
owner: Neo4j, Inc. (code owned by Neo4j Sweden AB)
release_cadence: monthly CalVer releases since 2025.01, each supported only until the next; 5.26 is LTS; next LTS 2026.LTS planned Nov 2026
license: Community GPLv3 (commercial agreement supersedes); Enterprise commercial; GDS OpenGDS GPLv3 plus closed code (EE needs licence file); Bloom activation key; NeoDash Labs Apache-2.0 unmaintained; n10s and APOC Core Apache-2.0; NVL licence UNVERIFIED (see LICENSE.txt)
redistribution_notes: CE is GPLv3, so bundling in a white-label appliance creates GPL distribution duties; EE needs a commercial agreement with OEM terms not public. EOIP ships only the client and no Neo4j binaries, Bloom or NVL.
legal_review_reason: GPLv3 Community Edition bundling duties; EE/OEM terms not public; NVL licence needs review
community_vs_enterprise: CE is single-instance only (GDS CE limited to 4 cores); EE adds RBAC, database-per-tenant, clustering and closed modules; Infinigraph sharding is a separate subscription not on Aura
resolution_note: neo4j:5-community resolves to the 5.26 LTS line, not the current release; GDS moved from 2.x to CalVer at 2026.03; NeoDash Labs unmaintained
action_reason: Assigned Tier A; required supported backend
decision_summary: INTEGRATE as supported backend behind GraphStore (customer-supplied, no binaries shipped); BUILD Cypher/GQL compiler, portable schema contract, tenancy and ACL; optional GDS and vector; REJECT n10s, Bloom and NVL embedding

name: Memgraph (with MAGE)
tier_reason: Candidate extra backend (Bolt/Cypher compatible) and direct competitor in GraphRAG/agent-memory positioning
release_cadence: roughly monthly minors with patch releases
license: Business Source License 1.1 (Additional Use Grant dated 2026-01-01 from v3.8.0) and Memgraph Enterprise License; Lab under proprietary Lab User Licence Agreement; MAGE Apache-2.0 up to v3.7.2 (archived repo), BSL since v3.8.0
redistribution_notes: BSL is not an open-source licence per its own text; bundling current Memgraph or MAGE is not assumed permitted. Treat as customer-licensed backend and never bundle.
legal_review_reason: BSL 1.1 additional-use grant change at v3.8.0 and MAGE relicensing from Apache-2.0 to BSL on repo merge
community_vs_enterprise: Database-per-tenant, RBAC/LBAC/PBAC and multiple non-default databases require Enterprise; Community gives one usable production database
resolution_note: Pricing page calls Community open source but licence text says BSL is not open source; MAGE merged into main repo at v3.8.0 and old repo archived; enterprise licence offline activation not verified
action_reason: Assigned Tier A; credible additional backend and competitor
decision_summary: INTEGRATE as optional customer-licensed Bolt backend (P2); BUILD deep-path pushdown IR, tenant placement, ACL-aware retrieval and OIDC MCP routing; EXPERIMENT in-engine vector/text; REJECT bundling current BSL MAGE

name: Kùzu and successors/forks (LadybugDB, RyuGraph, Bighorn)
tier_reason: Embedded columnar/CSR/worst-case-optimal-join architecture reference; upstream archived 2025 (Master Prompt section 5.1); not a supported EOIP backend
owner: Kùzu Inc. (archived); LadybugDB Developers for the main fork
release_cadence: none for Kùzu (archived); LadybugDB releases late Sep-Oct 2026
redistribution_notes: MIT allows OEM embedding and white-label redistribution with notice kept; the concern is operational, since embedding archived C++ means EOIP owns security patching.
legal_review_reason: No licence trigger; trigger is operational (patch ownership of archived code)
community_vs_enterprise: No enterprise edition; community fork governance is young
resolution_note: Kùzu repo archived 2025-10-10 (last release v0.11.3); LadybugDB is the only viable continuation; RyuGraph 2026 activity UNVERIFIED; Bighorn dormant
action_reason: Assigned Tier B architecture reference; archived upstream recorded
decision_summary: EXPERIMENT with LadybugDB as optional non-authoritative sidecar; BUILD CSR projection with WCO-style joins and algorithms in-house; REJECT Kùzu as backend adapter, DEFER LadybugDB adapter

name: ArangoDB
tier_reason: Multi-model (document + graph + search + vector) reference; licence change from Apache 2.0 to BUSL-1.1 directly relevant to EOIP redistribution
latest_version: 3.12.12 (latest patch in 3.12 series per release notes; 4.0 in development)
release_cadence: 3.12 patch series; 3.10 and 3.11 reached end of life 2025-05-30
license: Source: Business Source License 1.1 since 3.12 (previously Apache 2.0); prepackaged Community binaries: ArangoDB Community License (100 GiB dataset production limit, no commercial use or redistribution); Enterprise commercial
redistribution_notes: BUSL-1.1 forbids offering a commercial service giving third parties access to databases; Community License forbids commercial use and embedding. White-label bundling would need a negotiated Enterprise/OEM agreement.
legal_review_reason: BUSL-1.1 and Community License restrictions on commercial service and redistribution
community_vs_enterprise: Community License limits production to 100 GiB data and bars commercial use; Enterprise/OEM requires negotiated agreement
resolution_note: 3.12.12 release date unverified (Wikipedia lists 3.12.11 with conflicting August 2026 dates); offline operator/image mirroring not verified
action_reason: Assigned Tier B; licence change relevance
decision_summary: REJECT as bundled engine, DEFER as customer-licensed adapter; BUILD hybrid retrieval+traversal QueryPlan template and supply-chain licence gate; EXPERIMENT tenant-affine partitioning

redistribution_notes: Redistribution/OEM not permitted under published terms; Free EULA forbids sublicensing, derivative works and competitive evaluation; white-label embedding needs a negotiated OEM agreement.
legal_review_reason: Proprietary terms bar OEM/redistribution; Voicebox egress of query results to external LLMs
community_vs_enterprise: Free is evaluation-only; Enterprise via sales contract (terms UNVERIFIED)
resolution_note: Voicebox is a feature of one vendor, not a separate company; Karaoke on-prem appliance is historical; offline licence activation UNVERIFIED; no acquisition found
decision_summary: INTEGRATE customer-supplied Stardog as one more SPARQL backend; BUILD bounded RL/Datalog reasoning subset, explanation traces, R2RML import and grounded NL-to-query/abstention; REUSE pySHACL; EXPERIMENT tiered reasoning planner

community_vs_enterprise: Single OSS distribution; no enterprise edition
resolution_note: GitHub release page shows 18 Sep (PyPI date of 5.0.0.dev5); PyPI 2026-09-28 taken as authoritative; telemetry not verified

name: Senzing (embeddable real-time entity resolution SDK)
tier_reason: Leading embeddable real-time principle-based ER engine; benchmark for EOIP identity layer (BL-34/35/36)
members: Senzing SDK (C core with Python/Java bindings)
release_cadence: frequent; 4.4.0 2026-08-31, 4.4.1 2026-09-17, 4.4.2 2026-10-01; each minor line supported two years
license: Proprietary EULA 'May 2026.v1' (non-exclusive, non-transferable, no sublicensing, no distribution right, audit rights, no publishing performance comparisons)
redistribution_notes: Standard EULA bars distribution, sublicensing and third-party access, so EOIP cannot bundle it; use a customer-held licence or a negotiated OEM/partner agreement.
legal_review_reason: EULA bars distribution and benchmark publication; hardware ownership and audit clauses
community_vs_enterprise: Limited free use (source-record cap); production priced per Data Source Record (e.g. $58,560/yr for 10M DSRs); custom OEM terms by negotiation
resolution_note: Offline licence activation mechanics NOT PUBLICLY VERIFIED; SQLite limited to under 1M records, PostgreSQL for one-node
decision_summary: BUILD native real-time ER with merge/unmerge ledger and principle-based patterns; INTEGRATE Senzing as optional customer-licensed identity authority (legal review); REJECT white-label embedding under standard EULA
